title: Long Weekends in 2027: The India Leave Calendar and Where to Go
metaDescription: A planning guide to India’s 2027 long weekends — which holidays create three and four-day breaks, how to stretch them with leave, and where to travel.
excerpt: Two or three well-placed days of leave can turn 2027 into four separate trips. Here is the calendar, and what to do with it.
author: Trypinn Team
content:
The single highest-return travel habit for anyone with limited annual leave is looking at the year's holiday calendar in advance and booking around it. The people who get four trips out of six days of leave are not doing anything clever — they are just doing it in December instead of April.

Here is how to approach 2027, and what to do with each window.

## First, A Caveat Worth Reading

Indian public holidays are **not uniform**. The central government's gazetted list differs from state lists, many holidays are restricted rather than compulsory, and several — Eid, and festivals following the lunar calendar — are set by moon sighting and can shift by a day.

So treat any published calendar, including this one, as a planning framework and **confirm against your own employer's holiday list** before booking anything non-refundable. Your company's calendar is the one that matters.

## The Windows Worth Planning Around

**Republic Day — 26 January.** Falls on a Tuesday in 2027, which makes Monday the 25th a single-day-leave four-day weekend. This is the highest-value leave day of the year and it will be recognised by everyone, so book early.

**Holi — early March.** Check the date against your state's list. Holi weekends drive enormous domestic travel demand and the trains fill months ahead.

**Good Friday — late March.** Automatically a three-day weekend. Add the Thursday and you have four days, at a time of year when the hills are pleasant and the plains are not yet punishing.

**Ram Navami and Mahavir Jayanti — mid-April.** The clustering here is the best of the year in some states, with the potential for a genuinely long break from very little leave. Check your state's list carefully; this one varies.

**Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.** Dates are subject to moon sighting, so keep these flexible. Both frequently fall adjacent to a weekend.

**Independence Day — 15 August.** Falls on a Sunday in 2027, which unfortunately means no long weekend. Some organisations grant the Monday; most do not.

**Gandhi Jayanti — 2 October.** A Saturday in 2027. Again, no natural long weekend.

**Diwali — late October/early November.** The big one. Diwali falls on a Friday in 2027, creating a natural long weekend, and the surrounding week is the single busiest travel period in the Indian calendar. If you want to travel then, **book four to six months ahead.** Flights and trains at Diwali do not get cheaper as the date approaches.

**Christmas — 25 December.** A Saturday in 2027. The week between Christmas and New Year remains the most expensive travel window of the year regardless.

![India travel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1564165493092-36abd34c62ad?fm=webp&w=1200&q=60)

## The Strategy

**Book the January and April windows first.** They are the best-value long weekends and the least contested internationally, so international fares are reasonable.

**Treat Diwali as a different category.** It is not a long weekend to optimise; it is a peak season to either book very early or deliberately avoid. Travelling domestically during Diwali week means premium prices and full trains. Travelling internationally is often cheaper than travelling within India that week.

**Look for Tuesday and Thursday holidays.** A Tuesday holiday plus Monday's leave gives four days. A Thursday holiday plus Friday's leave does the same. These are where two days of leave generate eight days of holiday across a year.

**Book flights the day the calendar is confirmed.** Long-weekend fares on popular domestic routes rise steeply and do not come back down.

## Where to Go: Three-Day Weekends

Three days means a maximum three-hour journey each way. Realistic options from the major metros:

**From Bengaluru** — Coorg, Chikmagalur, Wayanad, Gokarna, Hampi, Pondicherry, Ooty, Sakleshpur, Yelagiri, BR Hills

**From Mumbai** — Alibaug, Lonavala and Khandala, Matheran, Kashid, Ganpatipule, Tarkarli, Nashik wine country, Daman

**From Delhi** — Rishikesh, Jim Corbett, Nainital, Mussoorie, Kasauli, Neemrana, Bharatpur, Agra, Alwar

**From Chennai** — Pondicherry, Yercaud, Tranquebar, Mahabalipuram, Kodaikanal, Chikmagalur by overnight

**From Hyderabad** — Hampi, Srisailam, Bidar, Gandikota, Papikondalu, Nagarjuna Sagar

**From Kolkata** — Mandarmani, Digha, Shantiniketan, Sundarbans, Darjeeling by overnight

![India travel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1571318393848-1a9d3b31a1bf?fm=webp&w=1200&q=60)

## Where to Go: Four-Day Weekends

Four days opens up flights and genuinely different regions:

**Domestic** — Goa, Kerala's backwaters, Udaipur, Jaisalmer, Rishikesh and the Garhwal hills, Kashmir in spring, Andamans if you fly early and late, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Ladakh in the summer months, Spiti in high summer

**International, from Indian metros** — Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Dubai, Muscat, Bali if you take one extra day

For a four-day international trip, the visa position matters enormously. Nepal requires nothing, Thailand, Malaysia, Sri Lanka and the Maldives are visa-free or simple visa-on-arrival for Indian passport holders, and Bhutan needs a permit rather than a visa. These are the destinations that work at short notice.

## Stretching a Long Weekend Properly

- **Take the last flight out on the working day before**, not the first flight on day one. You gain an entire morning
- **Return on the last flight of the final day**, not the morning after
- **Go one region, not three.** A four-day trip that visits three towns is a transport schedule
- **Book accommodation with free cancellation immediately** when the calendar is confirmed, and decide later
- **Hand luggage only.** On a three-day trip, a checked bag costs you two hours
- **Pick somewhere with a short transfer from the airport.** A ninety-minute drive each way removes half a day from a four-day trip

## A Realistic Year

Six days of leave, placed well, buys roughly:

- A four-day January break
- A four-day break around Good Friday
- A four or five-day break in April
- A long weekend somewhere in the second half of the year

That is four trips. The same six days taken without reference to the calendar produces one slightly longer week and three ordinary weekends.

The only real work is doing it early — the good windows are obvious to everyone, and the prices reflect how far ahead people booked. Putting the year's candidate windows into a shared plan in January, with a destination pencilled against each, is the difference between a year of trips and a year of intentions. **Trypinn** works well for this: block out the windows, let the group react, and book the ones that stick.
